title: Lifecycle has six path states plus two out-of-path states
context: Alternative approaches: simpler state machine; unlimited states; branching paths.
decision: Nodes move through 6 path states: draft → specified → assigned → implemented → reviewed → accepted. Two out-of-path states exist: `stale` (entered when upstream contract changes) and `deprecated` (entered when node is superseded). No other state exists.
consequences: Clear path from creation to acceptance; branching points enforce policy (e.g., only humans can accept); staleness is a system-triggered state, not manual; deprecation is orthogonal to the path; every transition is recorded with actor, time, and reason.
